outcome: Adaptive functioning status (Vineland-3 Adaptive Behavior Scales: communication, daily living skills, socialization, maladaptive behaviors)
cohort: The study included 39 individuals (22 males, 17 females) with genetically confirmed KBG syndrome from 36 unique families.
finding: Individuals with KBG syndrome displayed lower overall adaptive behavior composite scores compared to the general population, with those having epilepsy exhibiting generally lower scores, though statistical significance was only achieved in the written communication subdomain.
cross-section timing: Assessments were conducted at a single point in time via videoconferencing for individuals with genetically confirmed KBG syndrome.
